subsystems.name: Energy supply
subsystems.role: deliver the colossal, concentrated energy needed to create mass at all.

subsystems.name: Energy-to-matter converter
subsystems.role: turn photons or kinetic energy into particle–antiparticle pairs.
parts: photon–photon collision region or high-Z conversion target

subsystems.name: Antimatter handling
subsystems.role: deal with the fact that pair production yields as much antimatter as matter.

subsystems.name: Atom placement stage
subsystems.role: position individual atoms into the intended structure — the only part resembling a real factory.

subsystems.name: Blueprint compiler
subsystems.role: translate a digital design into an exact sequence of atom placements.

subsystems.name: Containment and safety
subsystems.role: keep vacuum, radiation and stray antimatter from destroying the machine.

buildSteps.title: Compile the blueprint
buildSteps.detail: A digital design is converted into an atom-by-atom map: which element goes where, and in what bond.

buildSteps.title: Generate the energy
buildSteps.detail: Roughly 9×10^16 joules — the output of a large power station running for years — is needed per kilogram of matter, so an enormous and controllable energy source comes first.

buildSteps.title: Convert energy into particles
buildSteps.detail: High-energy photons or particles are collided so that pair production creates matter and antimatter together.

buildSteps.title: Separate and trap the antiparticles
buildSteps.detail: Magnetic fields steer antiprotons and positrons into traps; if they touch ordinary matter they annihilate back into energy.

buildSteps.title: Assemble nuclei and atoms
buildSteps.detail: This is the hard step. Building elements from bare nucleons would require fusion and neutron capture cascades; a more tractable route is to take existing atoms and move them one at a time.

buildSteps.title: Place atoms into the structure
buildSteps.detail: Probe or optical manipulators position each atom, with the surface cooled so the pattern does not immediately rearrange.

buildSteps.title: Bond and verify
buildSteps.detail: The structure is annealed or chemically bonded into a solid, then checked with electron microscopy against the blueprint.

buildSteps.title: Scale up
buildSteps.detail: Going from a few thousand atoms to everyday objects would need a throughput and energy budget many orders of magnitude beyond any laboratory.

prerequisites.why: observed routinely in accelerators, but only as sparse particle–antiparticle pairs, never as bulk matter.
antihydrogen has been trapped in laboratories for minutes; industrial-scale storage does not exist.
atoms have been positioned individually with scanning probes and self-assembled with DNA origami, but only at nanoscale.
the energy cost of creating matter from energy is set by E=mc² and cannot be reduced by engineering.
no software today can specify a macroscopic object as an exact atomic assembly plan.

pathway.milestone: laboratory manipulation of individual atoms and molecules
pathway.unlocks: proof that matter can be positioned with atomic precision, at tiny scale.

pathway.milestone: nanoscale assembly of useful materials and devices atom by atom
pathway.unlocks: manufacturing of small components with designed atomic structure.
would require colliders and energy supplies orders of magnitude beyond present machines, and it produces equal antimatter.
instant object manifestation — for now, this remains speculation, and the practical route to it, if any, is atomic assembly rather than converting pure energy into objects.
